hook: An equation like 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂ is a recipe written in shorthand. A particle diagram is the same recipe drawn: you can count every atom and see which ingredient is left on the counter when the cooking stops. The exam asks you to move between the two, both ways.

prereq.q: Balance __CO + __O₂ → __CO₂. What are the coefficients, in order?
prereq.why: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂: 2 C and 4 O on each side.

prereq.q: In a particle diagram, two joined circles of the same color most likely show
options: a molecule of an element, such as O₂
two separate atoms of a compound
prereq.why: Two atoms of the same element bonded together are a molecule of that element.
A dissolved ionic compound is separate cations and anions.

figure.caption: Reading a reaction particle diagram. The particles used, not the particles present, give the coefficients; whatever is left over was in excess.

chain.cause: Atoms are rearranged, never made or destroyed
chain.effect: a correct diagram has the same count of each kind of atom before and after

chain.cause: Coefficients give the ratio in which particles react
chain.effect: the change in each count, not its starting value, gives the coefficients
the other reactant still appears in the After box

chain.cause: State symbols tell how each species exists
chain.effect: a diagram shows gases spread out, solids packed, and dissolved ions apart in water

ideas: A reaction particle diagram draws the particles before and after. Every atom drawn before is drawn after.
Find coefficients from what was used and made (After minus Before), reduced to the smallest whole numbers.
The limiting reactant runs out first. A reactant still present After was in excess; leave it out of the equation.
State symbols: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) dissolved in water. Ionic solids are drawn as packed arrays, never molecules.

misconception.wrong: Write the equation with the numbers of particles drawn in each box, leftovers included.
misconception.right: The equation gives the reacting ratio. Use only the particles that reacted and formed, reduce to the smallest whole numbers, and leave the excess reactant out.

summary: A reaction particle diagram and a balanced equation say the same thing. Atoms are conserved between the boxes, the changes in particle counts give the coefficients, a leftover reactant was in excess, and state symbols say whether each species is a solid, liquid, gas or dissolved in water.
